races.name: Gowran Park Golf Optional Claiming Race

runners_data.name: If Not For Grace
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Liam Cusack who has a form note flagging late fade — the OR=120 rating looks lofty given a return of 8th and 15th in recent starts, and 51 days off is enough to concern despite simulated going runs going 2/2.|

runners_data.name: Contrite
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes over for D K Weld and that booking deserves respect — placed over 10f at Goodwood on Good, and the step to 8f here over firm ground looks a slight query but the yard are 2/15 in the last fortnight.|

runners_data.name: Jp's Express
runners_data.note: Very busy horse (10 days since last run, five starts at the trip) who has a win and a place over 8f on Good, but the amateur rider and a trainer going 1/14 in 14 days give realistic pause about this being the day it goes in.|

runners_data.name: Passage Of Power
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Joseph Patrick O'Brien with Dylan Browne McMonagle booked — a potent alliance — and the yard's 7/66 fortnight record underlines live participation; two runs only, modest form on paper but likely to compete hard for the early lead.|

runners_data.name: Star Of Beauty
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent-runner with four places from nine runs on Good, suits today's firm conditions (hg: visor worn), and Kildare Condon's 1/4 fortnight strike is modest but the horse has been placed at this trip repeatedly.|

runners_data.name: Bill Silvers
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer in visor who has only managed 0 wins and 0 places from 15 similar-going starts — low-grade form, Jamie Orr's claim helps carry the weight but hard to see a pathway from the back in this large field.|

runners_data.name: Buttermere Ridge
runners_data.note: True hold-up type placed into the midfield cluster on the map; the fade warning in recent form (0-9740) is consistent, and while it won over hurdles it has no flat win or place from 15 similar-going attempts — STYLE_FIT of 0.91 reflects the mismatch.|

runners_data.name: Liberate
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's raider ran 9th on its most recent Good ground start over 8f, but has a flat win to its name and p headgear fitted; holds a natural hold-up profile that the map has pushed forward — likely to be positioned further back than the redistribution suggests.|

runners_data.name: Zitkala Sa
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with cheekpieces fitted, placed third over 10f at Good, but has no win from five starts and is being shifted from its natural hold-up position into a midfield slot it may not naturally find — Shane Foley at least gives it a competent pair of hands.|

runners_data.name: Countertop
runners_data.note: Has a fade warning attached and the form reads 00-050 with no win or place on similar going from seven attempts — the redistribution into midfield rather than the true rear is a stretch, and the 7lb claimer (Terry Casey) adds little confidence.|

runners_data.name: Slight Of Foot
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer without a jockey named (likely amateur) who wears hood headgear and has run poorly on Good ground recently — only 5 days since last run, which is very quick, and the fade flag is backed up by three single-figure finishes in the last five.|

runners_data.name: Hastily
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has 1 win and 2 places from 15 similar-going runs but the most recent form reads 9-0009 — has been pushed into midfield from its natural hold-up position and the age profile on fast ground is a concern.|

runners_data.name: Macinamillion
runners_data.note: 307 days off the track is the headline here — last ran over extreme distances (18-20f), stepping back sharply to a mile, and the redistribution into midfield from a true rear position is a secondary consideration behind the fitness question after nearly a year absent.|

runners_data.name: Minaun View
runners_data.note: The most interesting of the redistributed hold-up horses: two recent wins over 8f on Good and a STYLE_FIT of 0.94 meaning it is likely to push forward and grab the kind of prominent pitch the map already anticipates — Patrick McGettigan's 5lb claim keeps the weight reasonable.|

runners_data.name: Hello Stacia
runners_data.note: Second confirmed front-runner alongside Passage Of Power — ran 3rd on last time out over 8f at Good, so there is form to work with, but the prospect of fighting Passage Of Power for the lead from the outset makes a solo lead very unlikely.|

runners_data.name: Land Of The Giants
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for Adrian McGuinness who has 1 win and 3 places from 15 similar-going attempts — finished 3rd over 8f on Good twice this term and Ronan Whelan takes the ride, keeping it realistic rather than exciting.|

runners_data.name: May Night
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old returning from 387 days off the track — regardless of the redistribution into midfield, that layoff on fast ground at this age is the primary concern, and the form before the break was modest (5/0/7/13/5).|

runners_data.name: Mythical Rock
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has finished in the first two from three of his last five runs on Good ground over 8f — visor fitted, Sean Davis rides, and a horse who repeatedly finds himself placed without winning has strong claims if the pace scenario sets up correctly.|

races.paceDynamic: Passage Of Power and Hello Stacia are the two confirmed front-runners in an 18-runner field on Good to Firm ground over a mile at Gowran Park, and with both likely to contest the early lead, the pace should be honest rather than crawling — neither has the dominance to dictate solo and both are rated OR=120, meaning neither will simply yield. The resulting contested gallop will stretch the field out early and drain stamina reserves, making it harder for hold-up horses to find the gaps they need in what is already a crowded mid-to-rear section. Star Of Beauty, Land Of The Giants and Mythical Rock are the genuine prominent types who can track the pace in a realistic position, while the bulk of the field — Minaun View, Liberate, Buttermere Ridge, Zitkala Sa, Countertop, Hastily, Macinamillion and May Night — are true hold-up horses redistibuted to midfield on the map because there are simply more closers than the race shape can accommodate at the back. The field holds considerably more rear-of-field types than can all get their natural position, and Minaun View (STYLE_FIT 0.94, two recent wins) and Liberate are the most likely to push forward and actually secure a better berth than the map implies. The contested pace and firm ground favour prompt, prominent racers who sit just behind the leaders and pounce inside the final furlong, rather than deep closers who will struggle to find daylight through this large field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Suits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Passage Of Power and Hello Stacia fight for the lead at a genuine gallop, setting up the race for those sitting just off the pace.
scenarios.body: The honest early tempo burns out both leaders before the turn for home, leaving Star Of Beauty, Land Of The Giants and Mythical Rock — who have tracked comfortably — to swoop entering the straight. Firm ground rewards these prominent types who save vital energy through the race rather than expending it from the front or needing to weave through traffic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Hold On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves more even and controlled than expected, allowing Passage Of Power or Hello Stacia to find a sustainable rhythm and conserve enough for the finish.
scenarios.body: One of the two front-runners gets a soft lead while the other fades, meaning the pace paradoxically moderates and the leader is never truly wound up — a familiar pattern in large-field maiden/claiming company. Passage Of Power, with Dylan Browne McMonagle aboard and the backing of Joseph Patrick O'Brien's yard (T14: 7/66), is the more likely beneficiary given the quality of the booking.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Break Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fierce enough to string the field wide and thin, opening gaps for the genuine closers who manage to find a clear passage.
scenarios.body: Minaun View is the standout candidate here given two recent wins at this course and distance, a STYLE_FIT of 0.94 suggesting it will push forward and grab a better position than the map credits; Contrite and If Not For Grace also carry claims if they can find clear daylight down the straight. The major risk is traffic — 18 runners on a mile on firm ground often means the gaps simply do not open in time for true rear-of-field types.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart/Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes significant interference early, with the contested pace creating bunching, fallers or position losses that scramble the predicted shape entirely.
scenarios.body: In an 18-runner field on a turning course, a ragged start or early crowding can neutralise class advantages and elevate horses who find a clear run from mid-division by luck as much as judgment. Bill Silvers and Jp's Express, both racing off low weights with little market pressure, could profit from the chaos if the field concertinas into the straight.

watchPoints.text: Passage Of Power and Hello Stacia are on a collision course for the early lead — watch the opening two furlongs to see if one folds immediately or if they sustain a genuine duel, as the outcome defines the entire race shape.

Minaun View is mapped to midfield but is a true hold-up type with two recent wins — if Patrick McGettigan pushes it forward early to escape the traffic, its run will come from a very different position than expected and could be a significant market mover.

With 18 runners on a turning mile course, watch for early congestion on the turn — horses like Countertop, Hastily and May Night, all genuinely rear-of-field types squeezed into midfield on the map, could cause interference or lose all momentum in the bunching.

Macinamillion (307 days absent, dropping from 18-20f to 1m) and May Night (387 days off) are significant fitness unknowns — if either shows signs of distress or is eased, it could affect the racing room of those nearby in the final straight.

Star Of Beauty's consistency on Good ground (4 places from 9 similar-going runs) is worth monitoring for sectional position through the first half-mile — if it travels prominently without undue pressure, it is best placed to exploit whichever scenario unfolds.

races.name: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden
FINAL FURLONG PODCAST WITH 1XBET Handicap

runners_data.name: Alfred Tennyson
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's 4yo has won over this 7f trip on Good ground and arrives just 5 days post-run in decent nick, but his natural front-running aggression is likely to be frustrated here with Pretty Omagh Girl already installed at the head of affairs, meaning he may race less prominently than he'd prefer and his style-fit discount applies.

runners_data.name: Pretty Omagh Girl
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the ride on the confirmed pace-setter, who returns from a 45-day break with a proven win at 8f on Good ground and a clear tactical advantage as the uncontested leader; dropping back to 7f on a flat, fast track suits a horse who can settle and quicken rather than grind.

runners_data.name: Indigo Dream
runners_data.note: Shane Foley's mount has placed three times on similar ground but has shown a tendency to travel prominently and find limited late; the 35-day break and 137lbs are manageable, and a position just off the leader gives her every chance to pick up the pieces if the front-runner weakens.

runners_data.name: Ohailbhic
runners_data.note: Ronan Whelan partners this 5yo who has won twice over 8f at Sligo on Standard, but similar-going form at 7f on Good shows only modest returns (8/15 sim-going, no win); the hold-up style suits a stronger pace than is likely here.

runners_data.name: Lohoobb
runners_data.note: W J Lee takes the ride on this 3yo who races just three days since his last run, and while his natural instinct is to come from behind, the redistribution means he is effectively mapped in midfield against his preference; his sim-going record on Good is strong (9/9) but a lack of wins and a style not ideally served by a controlled pace limits his prospects.

runners_data.name: Little Empire
runners_data.note: Anthony McCann's 6yo has placed regularly over 7f on Good ground and will be ridden prominently by apprentice Patrick McGettigan (5), making him a logical place contender if he can tuck in behind Pretty Omagh Girl and produce a clean late effort; his 139lbs weight is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Exquisite Acclaim
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle's 7yo arrives wearing a visor and has been out of the frame in the majority of similar-going appearances (5/15); best form has come over 8f on Soft, and a hold-up style on a flat fast 7f in a race unlikely to produce strong pace makes this a difficult profile to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Pretty Omagh Girl is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the gates on Good to Firm ground over Gowran's flat 7f. Alfred Tennyson is a natural prominent type who will press forward but, with Little Empire and Indigo Dream also wanting to race close to the pace, there is competition for the early berths that could see Alfred Tennyson slightly squeezed back from his preferred spot. This field carries more prominent-running types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate — Pretty Omagh Girl is best placed to secure the front, with Little Empire and Indigo Dream most likely to hold the next positions, while Alfred Tennyson may find himself racing less forwardly than ideal. A sustainable, uncontested lead on a flat, fast track suits a prominent racer who can maintain rhythm throughout — horses tracking the pace in second or third without over-exerting early are the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Pretty Omagh Girl dictates an even, uncontested gallop and the closers are left with too much to do from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Pretty Omagh Girl, fresh off a 45-day break and proven at 8f, drops back to 7f on a flat, fast track and controls the pace entirely, with Ben Coen able to conserve energy before quickening in the final furlong; Little Empire and Indigo Dream track and pick up to fill the places.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Pretty Omagh Girl sets just enough gallop that a well-placed tracker can cruise into contention and outsprint her in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Alfred Tennyson or Indigo Dream, sitting a length or two off the leader without undue pressure, hit the rising ground fresh and burst past a leader who has done all the work; the even tempo means no one is exhausted but the horse with the better finishing kick under a confident hold-up ride wins.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that the front runners tie each other up and Ohailbhic or Exquisite Acclaim storm through from the rear.
scenarios.body: Ohailbhic, whose recent wins came over 8f at Sligo, would need to find the pace unusually strong for 7f at Gowran to get competitive; Exquisite Acclaim carries headgear concerns and has been out of the frame in most similar-going runs, making this scenario dependent on an untypically fast early pace that the runner data does not strongly support.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types battle vigorously for position early, burning out the front rank and gifting late runners a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: Lohoobb, a genuine hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to redistribution, is the natural beneficiary if attrition at the front creates a late opening; however, this scenario requires a contested early pace that Pretty Omagh Girl's likely untroubled lead makes improbable, and Lohoobb's style_fit discount further reduces the case.

watchPoints.text: Pretty Omagh Girl (Ben Coen) goes unchallenged to the front — watch whether any of Alfred Tennyson or Little Empire attempt to press her early, as any disputation of the lead is the single biggest threat to her dominance.

Alfred Tennyson's early position is key: if Chris Hayes is forced to settle further back than a length or two off the lead, his chance diminishes sharply given his natural prominent style being compromised by the field shape.
Ohailbhic's last two wins came at 8f on Standard at Sligo — watch whether he finds the 7f on Good to Firm too sharp and the pace insufficient to bring him into the race late.

Lohoobb runs just 3 days after his last start — monitor market moves for any sign of stable confidence, but be aware the hold-up style is poorly placed in this pace scenario and his redistribution to midfield is not his natural operating zone.

Little Empire with apprentice claimer Patrick McGettigan (5) could benefit from a 5lb weight reduction — if the pair settle cleanly in second or third, the claim is a live tactical advantage in a small 7-runner field.

races.name: Darley Irish EBF Hurry Harriet Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Hollys Graces
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator for De Bromhead and Colin Keane, but pushed into a midfield mapping in this shape because the field is rear-heavy; recent form reads 970-82, her sim-going record is modest (4/7, 0W1P), and stepping back to 1m1½f after several runs at 10-12f could help — but she will not get her natural stalking position here, which tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Lemsairbat
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's confirmed front-runner comes here 52 days freshened up with a solid OR of 98 and a consistent placing record (six places from 15 sim-going runs); the danger is she ignites an overly fierce duel with Star Performer that flatters neither, and her 0W from 15 sim-going starts tells its own story about converting.

runners_data.name: Moonlit Sun
runners_data.note: Henry de Bromhead's three-year-old is a natural hold-up filly — a race-winning closer who found traffic trouble at 8f on Good ground on debut — but the density of back-markers means she will be swept into midfield, not her preferred last-to-first berth; only three career runs, all on Good, and stepping sharply up in class here.

runners_data.name: Skydance
runners_data.note: McCreery's filly has a compelling sim-going record of 7/7 with one win and five places, and her recent form (5-13) shows improvement at 8f; stepping up to 1m1½f is the key question, but her hold-up style on a flat course with a long straight gives her a plausible route through if the pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Star Performer
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's unexposed three-year-old bolted up on debut over 9f Good at Gowran — the same track and similar ground — and her OR of 120 is comfortably the joint-highest in the field; Declan McDonogh takes the ride and her natural front-running style means she dictates, but she must prove she can handle a genuine lead battle rather than a solo procession.

runners_data.name: Subsonic
runners_data.note: Murtagh's four-year-old runs in a tongue-plate and has a checkered recent record — 71-387 — with her one win coming on Soft, and five of her eight sim-going runs failing to produce a place; the trip is fine but her form inconsistency and the class of the opposition make her vulnerable despite a midfield running style.

runners_data.name: Classiest
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's promising filly won on debut at the Curragh over 8f on Heavy and has been off 289 days — this is a significant absence and a sharp step up in class and distance; Ronan Whelan rides and the prominent style maps perfectly to this race shape, but the layoff and the jump to Listed level demand a significant fitness and class leap on return.

runners_data.name: Minerva
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's second string for Lordan has run six times, won over 7f Good and placed four times, showing gritty consistency; she steps up to 1m1½f for the first time and, while the prominent style suits the shape ideally, her best form has come at shorter distances and that trip question must be answered before she can be fully trusted.

races.paceDynamic: Star Performer and Lemsairbat are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset, creating a genuinely competitive early gallop on Good to Firm ground at Gowran over 1m1½f — neither is likely to concede without a fight. This contested pace will stretch the field into a line, ensuring the race is run at an honest tempo throughout rather than producing a late sprint off a slow gallop. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Hollys Graces and Moonlit Sun are true closers who are unlikely to secure their natural position and will instead race in midfield, diluting any late surge from the back. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can settle just off the contested duel and pounce once the pace-setters tire in the final two furlongs, making Classiest and Minerva — both naturally prominent — the stylistically best-placed profiles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Star Performer and Lemsairbat fight it out up front and the honest gallop sets up perfectly for a prominent stalker to swoop
scenarios.body: The contested front-running duel burns both leaders up by the two-furlong pole, leaving a well-placed prominent runner to pick up the pieces with a class-driven finish on Good to Firm ground

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Converts
scenarios.trigger: If Star Performer dictates without being seriously pressured and the pace settles to a rhythm he can control
scenarios.body: Star Performer, trained by Joseph O'Brien and partnered by Declan McDonogh, showed impressive authority on debut and his superior OR of 120 gives him scope to dominate if Lemsairbat fails to sustain the challenge; a front-runner who leads a steady-to-honest gallop and quickens from the front is entirely plausible on this ground

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Movers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace is strong enough to open up gaps in the straight and a midfielder can thread through with a sustained run
scenarios.body: Skydance has been consistent in similar going (7/7 sim-going record) and is stepping up in trip having won over 8f, giving her a plausible profile to motor through on the wide-open Gowran straight; Subsonic also has winning form on soft ground but her headgear and inconsistent form make her the speculative option here

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so strong that the field strings out and the redistributed hold-up types find clear daylight late from midfield
scenarios.body: Hollys Graces and Moonlit Sun are genuine hold-up horses but both are racing out of their natural role, mapped into midfield rather than the rear where they would ideally be; even if the pace collapses the field, the style-fit discount is significant and this scenario depends on too many things going right for types who cannot get their preferred berth

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Star Performer or Lemsairbat blinks first in the opening furlong — if one concedes and the other leads unchallenged, the race shape shifts decisively toward a front-runner scenario rather than the contested duel the pace map predicts.

Classiest returns from 289 days off and, while her prominent style is tailor-made for this shape, any sign of rustiness in her warm-up or early behaviour would significantly undermine her chances as the key pace-shape beneficiary.

Skydance is unproven beyond 8f — monitor how she travels through the first half of the race; if she is being pushed along before the home turn, the 1m1½f trip is likely to find her out on this Good to Firm surface.

Moonlit Sun and Hollys Graces will almost certainly not secure their natural hold-up positions — watch how far back they actually end up and whether any late run materialises, as it would require an unusually strong pace collapse to bring them into serious contention.

The Good to Firm conditions at Gowran (confirmed across all races on the card) will keep the gallop honest and the ground rattling; any horse with a going preference for softer ground — notably Lemsairbat, whose two wins came on Soft — should be monitored for comfort level early in the straight.

races.name: McEnery Cup Handicap

runners_data.name: Dallas Star
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Robson De Aguiar who will press for the early lead; shaped well in defeat over this trip and going (2nd and 3rd placings), but 53 days off adds a small query and faces a genuine pace duel with Marazion from the jump.

runners_data.name: Fixation
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's four-year-old drops back in trip from recent starts and has placed twice over 8f on Good, suggesting the stamina question at 1m4½f is open; Coen takes the mount and the hood (headgear) may sharpen focus, but the shorter-trip form profile makes this a task.

runners_data.name: Royal Hollow
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides this consistent eight-year-old who has placed five times at similar trips on Good ground and is a natural hold-up horse — the strong pace scenario is exactly what he needs, though five placing-without-winning runs at this level raises the familiar question of how badly he wants it.

runners_data.name: Marazion
runners_data.note: Shane Foley's mount is a progressive four-year-old who won over 1m2f on Good and placed over 1m4f; she races prominently and is well suited by quick ground, and if she secures a clear lead early rather than fighting Dallas Star, this trip and going combination looks very much in her favour.

runners_data.name: War Rooms
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride on this hold-up specialist whose sole recent win came over 1m3f on Good; he is a genuine hold-up horse who needs the pace to be genuine, and this race shape — three front-runners slugging it out — sets up perfectly for his late run if he gets a clean passage.

runners_data.name: Obscenity
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's four-year-old holds two wins and a place on Good ground at around this trip, making the ground and distance profile solid; rides with a visor and sits in midfield naturally, meaning he benefits from a strung-out field rather than a bunched cavalry charge.

runners_data.name: Star Harbour
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness's eight-year-old has placed five times this season on Good ground without winning, running in prominent style with a visor; consistent but elusive in front, this trip is a stretch on recent evidence where most starts have been over 1m2f.

runners_data.name: Navy Waters
runners_data.note: McCreery's five-year-old has placed consistently on Good ground, including a third over 1m6f which suggests stamina is not a concern; the visor is retained, and he tracks pace rather than sits deep, making him a potential beneficiary if the midfield scenario materialises.

runners_data.name: Daboya
runners_data.note: Donohoe's five-year-old has won twice recently and is a genuinely quick, front-running type — the blinkered runner would naturally want to race up with the pace but, with Dallas Star, Marazion and Ephesus all pressing for the lead, Holohan (7lb claim) is likely to find himself pushed back to a position that does not suit this horse's natural game.

runners_data.name: Sea Coral
runners_data.note: Harrington's four-year-old has placed on Good ground at this trip and wears a tongue-strap; a hold-up horse who has shown she stays, but recent form has been modest and she may need a particularly dramatic pace collapse to get competitive here.

runners_data.name: Ephesus
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's five-year-old is a confirmed front-runner wearing tongue-strap and hood, but recent form over 1m2f to 1m6f on Good has been poor (single-digit finishes throughout), and a 10lb claimer in Jared Huggan adds to the concern that he is simply here to ensure pace rather than to feature at the business end.

races.paceDynamic: Dallas Star, Marazion, and Ephesus all want to lead, guaranteeing a strong, genuine gallop from the outset over this 1m4½f trip on Good to Firm ground at Gowran. With three confirmed front-runners competing for the same real estate, the pace is unlikely to be controlled or tactical — expect Ephesus (lowest-rated of the trio, ridden by a 10lb claimer) to be outgunned for position, with Dallas Star and Marazion most likely to dominate the early stages and ensure the race is truly run throughout. This strong tempo over an extended trip on quick ground is a stamina examination and systematically favours hold-up horses and strong-staying midfielders who can conserve energy before a sustained finish — prominent racers who get caught in the early battle will be vulnerable late. The field also contains more naturally prominent types than the pace map can accommodate; Daboya, a genuine front-runner in normal circumstances, is unlikely to secure a forward pitch here and will race further back than ideal, discounting its prospects in any scenario that depends on a prominent position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Dallas Star and Marazion fight it out up front and the genuine gallop burns off the prominent challengers in the straight.
scenarios.body: The relentless early tempo over 1m4½f on Good to Firm leaves horses who raced prominently emptying in the final two furlongs, allowing genuine hold-up horses to pick up the pieces with a sustained late run. Royal Hollow and War Rooms, both proven hold-up types who relish this trip and going, are ideally placed to benefit from this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Aids Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Marazion or Dallas Star gains a clear lead early and the field strings out, removing the pressure of a sustained contested gallop.
scenarios.body: One of the front-runners settles into a rhythm unchallenged after the early scramble resolves, dictating terms and preserving enough energy to kick clear in the straight. Marazion, a course-proven winner stepping back up to 1m4f and trained by a hot yard, is the most likely to exploit this if she secures the rail and dictates.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Sweeper Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fierce enough to flatten both leaders and hold-up horses come with too wide a run, leaving a well-positioned midfield horse to thread through.
scenarios.body: Runners tracking the pace in a handy midfield position avoid both the early war and the wide late run, arriving at the perfect time in the straight. Obscenity and Navy Waters, both horses with form at this trip on this going who tend to travel well in midfield, are the profiles that benefit most from this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail To Close
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves more moderate than anticipated once Ephesus is dropped back early, allowing front-runners to coast through in a falsely run race.
scenarios.body: Without a genuinely punishing tempo, the hold-up horses lack the acceleration to reel in fresh leaders who have conserved energy, and prominent racers who track the front pair find themselves with a clear advantage entering the straight. Fixation, well-ridden by Ben Coen and capable of a prominent position, is the type to benefit alongside Star Harbour.

watchPoints.text: Dallas Star and Marazion are on a direct collision course for the lead — watch the first furlong to see which cedes and which dictates, as that resolution shapes the entire race.

Ephesus with a 10lb claimer in a three-way pace battle is a vulnerability to monitor; if he goes too hard early and capitulates before halfway, it could scramble the pace profile and give the race a deceptive middle section.

Daboya's natural front-running instincts versus a field that cannot give him space — if Holohan tries to force the position anyway, it could create traffic and interference in the early stages for those immediately behind.

Royal Hollow and War Rooms are both genuine hold-up horses whose finishing runs will be triggered by the pace being truly honest — watch whether Andrew Slattery positions Royal Hollow to get a clear sight of the straight without cover, as a clean early run from the back is essential.

Obscenity's visor and form record on Good ground at this trip make him interesting in the midfield scenario — watch where McMonagle positions him in the first half-mile, as any wide berth late will cost a horse of his profile dearly.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Median Auction Maiden

runners_data.name: Believe Again
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up performer with a fade pattern in finishes, running from OR 120 off just 14 days; her natural closing style is squeezed here by a field of similar types, placing her in midfield against her instincts and making a winning run from her preferred deep position unlikely.

runners_data.name: Highlander Addict
runners_data.note: Stays extreme distances (best form over 16-17f) and drops sharply in trip to 9.5f here; has won at 17f on Good, but this shorter test may arrive too quickly for a horse who needs a truly run race to peel off the back.

runners_data.name: Lonelyharbourwall
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old from Dermot Weld's yard — powerful stable form at 2/15 over 14 days — but his only run came over 16f on Soft and this Good to Firm 9.5f trip is a significant unknown on both counts.

runners_data.name: Gliondar
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's three-year-old was placed on debut over 8f on Good, steps up in trip to a suitable 9.5f, and Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride for a stable hitting 7/66 — natural prominent style fits perfectly into the dominant race shape here.

runners_data.name: Jumpingthegun
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's gelding is the lone confirmed pace-setter; form reads 3-4-7 in reverse and his recent runs include a third over 12f on Soft, but as sole leader he controls the fractions and may simply steal an uncontested advantage at this level.

runners_data.name: Blue Orquidea
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan three-year-old whose two runs have produced a 13th and a 5th on fast ground; a natural hold-up type forced into midfield by the congestion of closers in this field, with a STYLE_FIT flag tempering confidence in a forward-finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Salamina
runners_data.note: Debutante from Joseph O'Brien's yard with no racecourse form and no going data — entirely unknown quantity, though the powerful stable angle commands respect and debut winners at this course are not uncommon in maidens of this nature.

runners_data.name: Socratea
runners_data.note: W McCreery three-year-old with a single run — 7th of 9 over 8f on Good — stepping up to 9.5f; the extra distance is a logical move but she has shown nothing substantial yet, and 49 days off adds to the uncertainty around her readiness.

runners_data.name: Storm Petrel
runners_data.note: Has placed twice in three starts at trips between 7-9f on Good, suggesting she handles the conditions, but her hold-up style is genuinely compromised in this shape — pushed into a midfield berth she may not want, reducing the chance of her best finish.

runners_data.name: Xirivella
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes over for Noel Meade's three-year-old who has run creditably twice at 8f on Good; the step to 9.5f looks like an improvement trigger, the prominent style is ideally suited to the pace shape, and Keane's booking elevates the profile significantly.

runners_data.name: Karrygrant
runners_data.note: John Murtagh's stable has posted 2/21 over 14 days and Ben Coen rides; Karrygrant's form — two placed efforts in eight runners — suggests a consistent type who handles Good, and the prominent style maps well onto a race likely to reward horses settled close to Jumpingthegun.

runners_data.name: Lord Darragh
runners_data.note: Single run of 6th over 8f on Good for a small yard (0/2 T14); stepping up in trip which could help, but the slim formbase and low trainer strike rate offer little to work with at this stage.

runners_data.name: One Cool County
runners_data.note: Ran 6th over 12f on Good last time out and now drops significantly in trip to 9.5f for a yard with a modest 1/4 T14 record; the hold-up profile on a shorter distance compounds the concern, as this track and trip may simply not suit.

runners_data.name: Rock Of Claremont
runners_data.note: A Oliver's three-year-old has placed at 8f on Soft and Good; the prominent style fits the likely race shape well, and stepping up from 8f to 9.5f is a sensible progression for a horse who has shown consistency without winning.

runners_data.name: Yogini
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's filly showed a 2nd on debut over 12f on Good, suggesting she stays, and drops in trip here to 9.5f under Gavin Ryan; the headgear flag (tongue strap/blinkers) points to a need for sharper engagement — midfield to late style could activate if the pace is truly slow.

races.paceDynamic: Jumpingthegun is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 15-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine rival willing to press for the lead — this means Rory Cleary can dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop from the front on genuinely Good to Firm ground at Gowran. With the pace uncontested, the fractions are unlikely to be truly searching, which compresses the field into a bunch and reduces the advantage for deep closers making ground from off the pace. The field nominally contains multiple hold-up types — Believe Again, Blue Orquidea, and Storm Petrel — but all three have been redistributed from the rear to midfield on the map because the race does not offer enough space at the back for them all; their true last-to-first profile is constrained here. This race shape favours horses who can travel prominently in the first three or four, keep Jumpingthegun within range, and then sprint clear in the straight — notably Gliondar, Xirivella, Karrygrant, and Rock Of Claremont — with hold-up runners facing an above-average risk of finding the steady early pace insufficient to generate the finish they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Jumpingthegun dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the race only quickens in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Rory Cleary controls fractions throughout, allowing horses settled just off the pace to coast into contention without expending energy, and the winner comes from the prominent group who tracked the leader within a length or two entering the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Burst From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely slow, the field bunches, and a midfield runner produces a sharp turn of foot in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A compressed, slow-run race creates a sprint-finish lottery off the home bend, and a horse with latent class sitting sixth to eighth can produce one clean effort to cut through.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Jumpingthegun establishes a significant lead early and the pace proves more genuine than expected, stretching the field.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to close the gap in the back straight, Jumpingthegun reaches the turn with enough daylight to resist challenges on Good to Firm ground that suits a free-going type.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace unexpectedly quickens mid-race and the prominent horses are stretched, leaving the race open for late finishers.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the redistributed hold-up horses — Believe Again, Blue Orquidea, Storm Petrel — to race in their natural deep position and produce sustained late runs, which is a low-probability outcome given how the race shape constrains them.

watchPoints.text: Jumpingthegun goes unchallenged to the lead — watch whether Rory Cleary elects to kick on turning in or waits, as the decision will determine whether this becomes a sprint finish or a test of stamina.
Gliondar and Xirivella both want to race prominently for high-profile yards — watch the first furlong for any traffic or crowding between the pair as 15 runners break from the gates.

Highlander Addict is competing over a trip (9.5f) well short of his best distance (16-17f) — if the pace is truly steady he may stay on from midfield late, but watch whether he gets competitive in time.
Salamina (O'Brien, debut) is entirely unexposed — watch market support in the final minutes before the off as a pointer to stable confidence in a genuinely unknown quantity.

Believe Again, Blue Orquidea, and Storm Petrel — all natural hold-up types — are mapped to midfield; watch whether any of them drift wider on the turn to find a clear passage, as a bunched finish could see them arrive late but too wide.

races.name: 1XBET IRISH SPIRIT Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: She's Ideal
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness's mare runs prominently and ran 3rd over 10f on good ground 23 days ago — the step back to 9f on good-to-firm suits, and tracking the uncontested leader from stall is her natural game; Sam Coen's claim adds tactical flexibility.

runners_data.name: Keilah
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator on turf whose recent form at 18f and 10f on good ground reads adequately but the drop to 9f looks sharp — Jack Cleary's inexperience in a 20-runner field compounds the navigation risk from deep.

runners_data.name: Perfect Judgement
runners_data.note: Hold-up style on good ground, but five successive finishes of 5th or worse including three 7ths on this going, suggest the rating has not caught up with the form line; Ronan Whelan's class is the only real upside here.

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll rides a genuinely prominent racer who ran just 8 days ago, suggesting connections are happy with his condition; his recent handicap marks over 8f on good going are modest but the step to 9f and a lone leader to track could flatter him.

runners_data.name: Giselles Defence
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden by Sean Davis, this hold-up mare showed one win on good ground but her turf headgear, SOF finishing positions, and a long losing run on this going type make meaningful improvement hard to project.

runners_data.name: Thompson Gunner
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on standard Tapeta but his four Irish starts all came on artificial surfaces — the switch to good-to-firm turf is a significant query; a genuine hold-up horse pushed to midfield on this map, and 145 days off the track adds further risk to an already unproven profile.

runners_data.name: Pimlico Piranha
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner and pace anchor, who has shown the ability to lead but fades in the finish — on good-to-firm over 9f with no rival to press, any chance is conditional on the field failing to close, and three career starts showing double-figure finishes are not encouraging.

runners_data.name: Tullyesker
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose Flat form spans only good and soft going at sprint trips — the redistribution to midfield on this map reflects the overcrowded rear, and three career runs without a place offer little to build a case on.

runners_data.name: Gold Dublooms
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose best recent effort was a 5th over 10f on good ground, but the form includes 12th and 9th on this going; headgear (hood/tongue) suggests a quirky profile, and the out-of-role positioning on the map tempers any expectations.

runners_data.name: Connova
runners_data.note: The most interesting of the redistributed hold-up horses — three consecutive 3rds over 10f on good ground show consistent placing form and Chris Hayes is a significant jockey booking; though naturally a closer, his Irish form on this going and trip gives him a live shout if gaps appear.

runners_data.name: Georg Zhukov
runners_data.note: Placed 2nd on only start over 10f on good ground but his subsequent form is unremarkable and he carries a Reserve rider; a true hold-up horse pushed into midfield by congestion at the rear, and the unresolved jockey situation is a practical concern.

runners_data.name: Pettus Bridge
runners_data.note: Prominent style but three runs all ending in 9th, 9th, 11th suggest the horse is not yet competitive at this level; fades in the finish tag and a Reserve rider mean this is firmly at the bottom of the betting interest.

runners_data.name: Bang Po
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type with a form string of 090060 — has never won on turf at this going and the redistribution to midfield masks a horse that wants to race much further back than it can in this field; Reserve rider adds nothing.

runners_data.name: Omissions
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle is an elite booking that demands attention, but three career starts all ending in 9th or worse on good ground over shorter trips, plus the fades-in-finish flag, mean the jockey upgrade is doing a lot of heavy lifting.

runners_data.name: No More Hiding
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse off a 59-day break whose best effort is a 7th — all five career starts are outside-the-frame finishes on various surfaces, and W J Lee's presence cannot mask a record that offers nothing for this distance or going.

runners_data.name: Shelbourne Flyer
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's gelding has placed twice over this trip on good ground wearing a tongue-tie/blinkers combination, showing he stays and acts — redistributed to midfield as a natural hold-up type in an overcrowded rear, but the course experience and headgear consistency give him marginal edge over similar types.

runners_data.name: Lohengrin
runners_data.note: A 6-year-old with a six-race losing run entirely on good ground at this sort of trip — the history speaks plainly; a hold-up horse placed out of natural role by the congested field, with a Siobhan Rutledge ride that carries no weight of money expectations.

runners_data.name: Onyeisi
runners_data.note: Karl Thornton's 3-year-old ran 4th over 10f on good ground in latest and has consistent form at this trip — Ben Coen is a live jockey booking and blinkers sharpen focus; a hold-up type in his natural element if the pace quickens and gaps emerge.

runners_data.name: Cameclose
runners_data.note: Placed 2nd over 10f on good ground on debut showing the ability is there, but three subsequent finishes of 8th/9th/9th tell a different story; a natural hold-up racer pushed into midfield by congestion, and the fades-in-finish flag limits the scenario where this position matters.

runners_data.name: La Campanella
runners_data.note: Gerard Keane's mare has placed 4th and 5th over 8-10f on good ground wearing hood and tongue-tie — she stays the trip and acts on the surface, but a hold-up style that cannot get its natural position in this field and a fades-in-finish flag combine to make her a minor player at best.

races.paceDynamic: Pimlico Piranha is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 20-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine rival willing to press for the lead — this means the pace will be controlled and moderate from the outset, with Pimlico Piranha dictating a sustainable gallop through the first half of this 1m1½f trip on good-to-firm ground. The danger is not being run off its feet but rather that a field packed with prominent and hold-up types will be coiled just off a falsely steady pace, setting up a sprint finish from the home turn. Prominent racers She's Ideal and William F Browne are best placed to track the leader and pounce, while the vast majority of the field — Georgia Zhukov, Cameclose, Thompson Gunner, Connova, Shelbourne Flyer and others — have been redistributed to midfield on this map because the sheer volume of hold-up types exceeds what can realistically race at the rear; in practice, several will push forward and create a bunched, contested middle section. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the uncontested leader, time their run from two furlongs out, and avoid the traffic that will engulf the overcrowded midfield-to-rear brigade.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Pimlico Piranha sets a controlled, uncontested lead and prominent racers track smoothly into the straight.
scenarios.body: Pimlico Piranha rolls along at a comfortable clip, giving She's Ideal and William F Browne a perfect gun-barrel sightline into the final two furlongs where their class advantage over the hold-up runners kicks in; the hold-up horses are caught in traffic as the pace quickens and simply cannot close the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pimlico Piranha Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and no prominent racer commits early enough to challenge before the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Pimlico Piranha bowls along unchallenged, conserving enough energy through a slow first half to resist weakened challenges from hold-up runners arriving late; the going-to-firm ground suits a horse that has at least shown early foot, and the lack of a pressing rival proves decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Thread Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply from halfway and the prominent runners are caught out, leaving gaps for the deepest closers.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected tempo from the outset — triggered if any of the redistributed hold-up types push forward and fight for early position — strings the field out and opens the race up for a genuine late finisher; Connova, who has placed consistently at this trip on good ground, and Onyeisi, who stays well, could thread through a tiring field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded middle section creates interference and the race is won by a horse that avoids trouble on the wide outside.
scenarios.body: With 20 runners on a tight course, multiple redistributed hold-up types pressing forward will generate bumping and crowding from the home turn, gifting a clear run to any horse that drifts wide early; this is the least predictable shape and depends on misfortune rather than class.

watchPoints.text: She's Ideal and William F Browne are the two prominent racers best positioned to exploit the lone uncontested front-runner — if either secures the rail or a clear position just off Pimlico Piranha's shoulder into the home straight, the race could be effectively over before the closers engage.

The sheer number of redistributed hold-up horses — Georg Zhukov, Cameclose, Thompson Gunner, Connova, Shelbourne Flyer, Bang Po and others — means at least four or five will push forward from their natural position, creating a compressed and potentially volatile mid-race bunch between 5f and 3f out.

Pimlico Piranha's fades-in-finish flag is significant in the context of being the sole pace-setter — if the moderate gallop it sets is slow enough to bring closers into play at the 2f pole, its chance dissolves quickly and the race opens up unpredictably.

Connova (Chris Hayes) and Onyeisi (Ben Coen) are the two hold-up runners with the strongest jockey bookings and the most consistent recent form over this trip on this going — monitor their starting prices as a market guide to whether the holding-up position in a pace-starved race is being backed at all.

Multiple Reserve riders (Georg Zhukov, Pettus Bridge, Bang Po) mean late jockey changes are possible, which could alter tactical plans for those horses and further disrupt the midfield positioning picture.

races.name: 1XBET IRISH SPIRIT Handicap (Div II)

runners_data.name: Miss Crinshawn
runners_data.note: Peter Fahey's hold-up operator, consistent in similar good-ground conditions (5 of 10 placed or better on this surface) but racing here over a shorter trip than her best recent form — will need a strong pace to close, which this shape may not provide.

runners_data.name: Walls Cross
runners_data.note: Consistent underperformer carrying the fade-in-finish flag; only three runs showing, all well behind, with zero placings on similar ground — limited evidence of an angle and likely to fill a minor role at best.

runners_data.name: Medieval Night
runners_data.note: W J Lee partners this hold-up type who has plentiful form on good ground (13 of 15 runs on similar going) but multiple recent efforts out of the frame — stepping back in trip slightly from recent runs suits, but needs a genuine pace to mount a challenge.

runners_data.name: Nibras Rainbow
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn's prominently-raced six-year-old with two wins on good ground in the past six starts and a profile that maps perfectly onto a race where a lone front-runner controls the gallop — most naturally placed of any horse in this field to pounce if Dancing Steve's pace softens.

runners_data.name: Urban War
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up performer with recent efforts over extreme distances (16f, 17f) before this 9f-equivalent task — significant trip drop is an unknown quantity and the good ground suits on historical form, though form is patchy.

runners_data.name: Brewel Hill
runners_data.note: Peter McCreery sends this ten-year-old veteran who races prominently and has shown a win and three placings from 12 good-ground starts — the prominent style is a genuine fit for today's race shape even at advanced age, and his consistency at this trip is a quiet positive.

runners_data.name: Thegooseiscooked
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride on this nine-year-old who is a natural hold-up horse but the crowded rear means he is likely to find himself in mid-division rather than his preferred spot — Keane's ability to find gaps is relevant, though one win and form that has dried up recently tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Nephin Mountain
runners_data.note: Michael Mulvany's three-year-old won at 10f on good ground and ran back just 10 days ago — the quick turnaround bears watching, and while he is a genuine hold-up type his redistribution into midfield means he cannot settle as deep as ideal; the Gowran win last time gives a course angle.

runners_data.name: Duchess Anne
runners_data.note: Mrs Denise Foster's mare has a single good-ground placing from eight runs on similar going and tends to come from behind — forced into a mid-division role by traffic, she faces the challenge of improving on a modest record without being able to get her natural position.

runners_data.name: Reponse Finale
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's hold-up runner returning from 68 days off and carrying the fade-in-finish concern — recent form was over much shorter trips (6f-8f) making this 1m1½f trip a question mark, and both absences and style mismatch weigh against.

runners_data.name: Shahada Ace
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery-trained four-year-old with a fade-in-finish flag, a poor recent run sequence (990006) and history of finishing well adrift on good ground (12 of 15 similar-going runs behind) — the style displacement into midfield adds another layer of difficulty.

runners_data.name: Winston's Promise
runners_data.note: Three runs only, all finishing 8th or worse, carrying headgear and a fade-in-finish warning — pushed into a mid-division role from a natural hold-up profile, this lightly-raced three-year-old looks unlikely to land a blow in a 20-runner field.

runners_data.name: Dancing Steve
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness's visor-wearing five-year-old is the lone mapped front-runner and will likely get an uncontested lead, but his form shows persistent fading late in races (0-0008 recent, 13th, 13th in recent starts) — the solo lead is a structural advantage that his finishing tendency may undermine.

runners_data.name: Rockbury Lad
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over on this seven-year-old, a genuine hold-up performer fitted with tongue-strap and pads, but his recent form on good and similar ground shows zero wins or placings from his last five — a top jockey booking is the main positive in an otherwise modest profile.

runners_data.name: Chapel Island
runners_data.note: Wesley Joyce's three-year-old has four starts showing consistent top-five or near finishes at longer trips (10f-13f) — dropping back in trip slightly from preferred distances, and the hold-up style in a compressed field means he must wait for room in the closing stages.

runners_data.name: Cleopatra's Needle
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes partners this eight-year-old hold-up operator who has placed twice in his last five on good ground and finished well at 8f-10f — the headgear (hood) and experience count, though the redistribution into midfield disrupts his preferred deep hold-up role.

runners_data.name: Invincible Destiny
runners_data.note: Shane Foley's three-year-old from the Harrington yard has only three runs all finishing 7th or worse over 12f — stepping well back in trip and carrying a fade-in-finish concern means she faces an uphill task, though a stable with 3 winners from 33 runners in 14 days is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Money Shuffler
runners_data.note: William Roper's six-year-old returns from 91 days off with all recent runs on artificial surfaces — the switch back to turf and good ground combined with a long absence and a mid-pack role make this a speculative contender at best.

runners_data.name: Chavajod
runners_data.note: A visor-fitted eight-year-old returning from 122 days off with a form string of 000-00 and a history of finishing near the rear on good and firm ground — the layoff, age and poor recent record make this an extremely difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Chou Chou
runners_data.note: Eamonn O'Connell's five-year-old has a win and placed efforts historically but recent form on good ground shows finishes of 13th and 14th — returning from 72 days off and displaced into midfield from a hold-up style, needs everything to go right to feature.

races.paceDynamic: Dancing Steve is the one confirmed front-runner in this 20-horse field and, critically, appears to face limited genuine pressure for the lead — Nibras Rainbow and Brewel Hill are the only other mapped prominent types, meaning Dancing Steve can slide into an uncontested, controlled gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m1½f at Gowran. With a sustainable pace set by a single, largely unchallenged pace-setter, the race is unlikely to turn into a true test of stamina and the tempo will almost certainly be insufficient to string out the field and exhaust mid-pack runners. The field holds significantly more hold-up and prominent types than can realistically secure their preferred positions: Rockbury Lad, Nephin Mountain, Winston's Promise, Thegooseiscooked, and multiple others are genuine hold-up horses who will find themselves shuffled into an already congested midfield, unable to settle where they want. This controlled, uncontested pace shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or in a handy mid-division position and use a strong cruising speed rather than a late, sustained finishing burst — pure closers dependent on a truly run race are at a structural disadvantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dancing Steve Dictates Gently
scenarios.trigger: If Dancing Steve leads throughout at a controlled tempo with Nibras Rainbow and Brewel Hill sitting just behind, creating a steadily-run contest.
scenarios.body: Dancing Steve controls fractions on Good to Firm ground, and the race develops into a sprint from 2f out where those travelling well in the first third of the field hold the edge; prominent types who can quicken under a sustainable pace are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just brisk enough to produce a two-furlong dash where handy horses who have been covered up within the first five or six lengths pounce.
scenarios.body: Nibras Rainbow and Brewel Hill, having raced in a prominent but covered position, get a clear run turning in and use their good-ground speed to hit the line strongly; both have demonstrated solid form at similar trips on quick surfaces and this shape suits their profiles directly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Get Lucky Break
scenarios.trigger: If a bunched mid-division breaks up early enough — due to traffic — to allow a genuine hold-up horse to find a clear run from 3f out.
scenarios.body: Nephin Mountain, Cleopatra's Needle or Miss Crinshawn find daylight in the closing stages after being shuffled wider than ideal, but the slow early gallop means they must make up ground on horses still travelling well; the compressed field still makes this difficult and the majority of redistributed horses are not racing in their true roles.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Dancing Steve sets a false pace that implodes inside the final 2f, leaving the race wide open to whichever horse survives the scrimmage from mid-division.
scenarios.body: With 20 runners on a flat track, traffic and interference become the dominant factor and the winner emerges from an unpredictable late scramble rather than a tactical shape; Dancing Steve's recent form shows consistent late-race fading which makes this non-trivial, though even here prominent types likely benefit from being first to the site of the breakdown.

watchPoints.text: Dancing Steve is the sole pace-setter in a 20-runner field — if he gets mugged for position approaching the first bend or drifts wide on a flat track, the entire pace dynamic collapses and the field races at a crawl, dramatically altering every scenario.

Rockbury Lad and Nephin Mountain, both genuine hold-up horses, have high-profile jockey bookings (Dylan Browne McMonagle and Terry Casey respectively) who may attempt to push forward and secure a better position — if they do, Dancing Steve faces more pressure than the map suggests.

With 20 runners on this track, bunching and traffic problems at the 3f-2f mark are a serious risk for mid-division horses; Thegooseiscooked and Miss Crinshawn in particular need clean runs that may not materialise in such a large field.

Nibras Rainbow's trainer Paul Flynn has zero wins from 21 runners in the last 14 days but the horse's form profile and prominent style are structurally well-matched to this race shape — watch for whether he contests the early position actively or drops back and waits.
